en: Taal Volcano emits sulfur dioxide gas, a state of matter that expands to fill the surrounding air.
Halo-halo is a heterogeneous mixture because you can easily see and separate its different ingredients like beans.
Burning sugarcane bagasse to produce ash and smoke is a chemical change because new substances form.
The seawater in the West Philippine Sea is a homogeneous solution containing dissolved salts and minerals.
Abaca fiber has high tensile strength, a physical property making it ideal for creating strong ship ropes.
The Banaue Rice Terraces are carved from solid earth, which maintains a definite shape and volume.
Smoking fish to make tinapa causes a chemical change that alters the proteins to preserve the meat.
Jeepneys run on diesel, a liquid mixture of hydrocarbons that flows and takes the shape of its container.
Melting ice into water at the Baguio Panagbenga Festival is a physical change that does not create new substances.
Adding sugar to calamansi extract creates a homogeneous solution when the solid crystals completely dissolve in the liquid.
Geothermal plants in Tiwi, Albay, use steam, a gas state of water, to spin turbines and generate electricity.
The Philippine one-peso coin uses nickel-plated steel, giving it specific physical properties like magnetism and corrosion resistance.
